canonical.title: Chora on foot: Kastro, the Portara and the town core

parent.title: Naxos in 3–4 days: what to do, in what order, and what to skip

siblings.title: Naxos beaches, coast by coast: which beach for which day
siblings.summary: The west-coast strip south of Chora carries a 3–4 day trip; the east coast and the remote south are day-eaters you should skip unless a boat or a specific obsession justifies them.

siblings.title: The Naxos interior: mountain villages, marble country and Mt Zas
siblings.summary: Two driving loops and one dawn climb cover the whole interior: the Tragaea (Demeter temple, Halki, Byzantine churches) in a day, Zas plus Apeiranthos in a second, the emery north as an optional third — with 2026 hours, prices and road realities.

siblings.title: Eating and drinking Naxian on a 3–4 day trip
siblings.summary: Naxos is the one Cycladic island that feeds itself — two PDO cheeses, a PGI potato, a PGI citron liqueur — and the eating is inland, not on the beach strip.

siblings.title: Naxos 2026: getting there, and whether you need a car
siblings.summary: Take the fast ferry from Piraeus, rent a car for 2 of your 3–4 days, and let the bus cover the beach days.

siblings.title: Naxos in 3–4 days: where to base yourself
siblings.summary: For a 3–4 night first visit, base in Chora (Naxos Town) — port, buses, dinner and a beach are all on foot; the beach strip wins only for a pure swim-and-sleep trip.

siblings.title: Day trips off Naxos: which one earns a day of four
siblings.summary: On a 3–4 day first visit, no off-island ferry day trip beats Naxos itself; the only day-boat worth booking is a local Small Cyclades cruise that never asks you to change islands.

sources.title: Municipality of Naxos — The Temple of Apollo (Portara)
sources.claim: Portara is the sole remnant of an unfinished 530 BC temple of Apollo begun by Lygdamis, four marble blocks of ~20 tons each, on Palatia islet linked to town by a paved footpath.

sources.title: Portara Naxos — opening hours
sources.claim: The Portara site is open-air, accessible 24/7, with free entry.

sources.title: Explore Naxos & Paros — Portara / Temple of Apollo
sources.claim: Portara is 5 minutes across the causeway plus 5 minutes uphill; extremely crowded at summer sunset; grippy shoes needed because the causeway gets slippery in choppy seas.

sources.title: Explore Naxos & Paros — Naxos Town (Chora)
sources.claim: Recommended order for Chora: old town early morning, Kastro mid-morning, promenade after 18:00, Portara in the last hour before sunset; don't drive into town; Portara is 25-30 min on foot from Agios Georgios; allow at least half a day.

sources.title: Greeka — Kastro of Chora, Naxos
sources.claim: Kastro founded 1207 by Marco Sanudo, pentagonal, reused ancient acropolis and Portara temple marble; free entry, still inhabited; 5-10 min walk from the waterfront or a free lift to Avaton 1739 cafe; Glezos/Crispi Tower is the only survivor of twelve and the only circular one; Kastro + Portara walk ~2.5 hours.

sources.title: Municipality of Naxos — Kastro of Chora
sources.claim: Kastro had three gates; Trani Porta (north) and Paraporti (south) survive; inside are the Della Rocca Barozzi tower museum, Tower of Crispi, Catholic Cathedral, Panagia Theoskepasti, Capuchin monastery, Archaeological Museum, Capella Kazatza and the Ursuline school.

sources.title: Municipality of Naxos — A tour of the Kastro district
sources.claim: Municipality's own walking order through the Kastro: Trani Porta, Della Rocca Barozzi tower, Tower of Crispi, Catholic Cathedral, Panagia Theoskepasti, Capuchin monastery, Archaeological Museum, Capella Kazatza, Ursuline school.

sources.title: Hellenic Ministry of Culture — Archaeological Museum of Naxos
sources.claim: Archaeological Museum of Naxos is closed for the 'Islet of Museums in the Castle of Chora' renovation; since 15 May 2021 a temporary exhibition runs on the second floor of the Saint Ursula Cultural Center, 09:00-14:00, closed Tuesday, free entrance.

sources.title: Hellenic Ministry of Culture — Site Museum of Naxos Mitropolis
sources.claim: Site Museum of Naxos Mitropolis was created in 1999 as Greece's first on-site museum of its type, nominal admission EUR 5, but the ministry listing states it is closed from 01.08.2025.

sources.title: Greeka — Mitropolis Museum, Naxos
sources.claim: The Mitropolis / Ancient Town Museum is listed as permanently closed.

sources.title: Municipality of Naxos — Venetian Museum
sources.claim: Della Rocca-Barozzi Venetian Museum in the Kastro opens daily 10:00-15:00 and 19:00-22:00, is shown by a staff member, and hosts musical events in its courtyard from April through October.

sources.title: TripHobo — Venetian Museum, Naxos
sources.claim: Venetian Museum entrance is around EUR 4 and the guided tour lasts about forty minutes, offered in English and Greek.

sources.title: Rough Guides — Naxos music festival
sources.claim: The Domus Festival of classical, jazz, choral, Byzantine and traditional music is held at the Venetian Museum; tickets booked in advance at the museum (22850 22387) and include a glass of local wine or kitron.

sources.title: Municipality of Naxos — Domus Festival at the Venetian Museum
sources.claim: The Domus Festival at the Venetian Museum runs concerts between April and October, including jazz, classical guitar and piano.

sources.title: Greeka — Catholic Cathedral of Naxos
sources.claim: The Catholic Cathedral stands on the central square of the Kastro, dates to the 13th century and is decorated with Naxian marble.

sources.title: Greeka — Orthodox Cathedral (Zoodochos Pigi), Naxos
sources.claim: The Orthodox Cathedral, dedicated to Zoodochos Pigi, was established around 1787 by Bishop Neophytos and stands next to the Grotta site on the north side of town.

sources.title: Municipality of Naxos — Archaeological site of Grotta
sources.claim: Grotta, on the north side of Naxos harbour below Mitropoleos Square, exposes part of the Mycenaean-era capital (~1300 BC) including agora and settlement, with some constructions now submerged in the sea.

sources.title: Greeka — Naxos Town (Chora)
sources.claim: Bourgos is the Greek quarter spreading around and below the castle walls, named from the Italian 'borgo'; the seafront district holds the bus station, banks, luggage storage and car rental offices.

sources.title: Airial — Bourgos Old Market quarter
sources.claim: The Bourgos Old Market quarter is a maze of narrow streets with shops and stalls; shops skew pricey and weekday mornings are the quiet window, late afternoon the prettiest light.

sources.title: The Common Wanderer — Naxos Chora guide
sources.claim: Chora deserves two or three days; visit before 9am or late afternoon; the old town is a rabbit warren of arches and marble streets; Agios Georgios is a five-minute walk south from the port; 520 is a rooftop bar in the old market overlooking the port and Kastro.

sources.title: Naxaki — Agios Georgios beach
sources.claim: Agios Georgios is about 1 km from the port and town centre, a flat 15-minute walk along the waterfront road, Blue Flag certified; morning secures the best positions before peak heat and late afternoon gives the best light.

sources.title: General Blue — Naxos sunrise & sunset times
sources.claim: Naxos sunset times in August 2026: 20:12 on 14 Aug, 20:04 on 20 Aug, 19:49 on 31 Aug.

sources.title: Greeka — Naxos bars
sources.claim: Named Chora bars include 520, The Naxos Apothecary, Oinochoros, On The Rocks and Prime.

sources.title: Travel Greece — Naxos nightlife 2026
sources.claim: Naxos nightlife is concentrated in Chora along the seafront and old-town streets, and bar-hopping there is walkable.

sources.title: Naxos.net — museums
sources.claim: The Archaeological Museum's permanent home is a five-storey 17th-century Venetian mansion; the Venetian Museum sits beside the north gate of the castle in the Della Rocca and Barozzi mansions.

sources.title: Cycladen.be — Chora Naxou
sources.claim: The Kastro's north-western entrance still contains its original wooden gate; the archaeological museum building is a former French college where Nikos Kazantzakis studied.

sources.title: Greeka — Portara of Naxos
sources.claim: The causeway to the Portara is about a 5-minute walk from town, and there is no lighting on the road at night.
